newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-U.S. farm subsidies aimed at EU - Farm Bureau.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-U.S. farm subsidies aimed at EU - Farm Bureau.

text.p: U.S. Farm Bureau president Dean Kleckner said on Tuesday that any potential retaliatory U.S. farm subsidies aimed at the European Union would not necessarily impact on Australian agricultural exports.

"If you look at Australian exports over a period of some years it's very difficult to see that our Export Enhancement Programme (EEP), or our export subsidies have really hurt them consistently," Kleckner told Australian Broadcasting Corp Radio.
The Farm Bureau is the largest farm group in the U.S.

Kleckner, also a senior trade adviser to U.S. President Bill Clinton, said while the U.S. has not used export subsidies for nearly two years he did not think that "throwing export dollars at certain markets would hurt (Australian) markets".
He said the dynamics of exporting were always changing and that there was a constant battle to maintain market share.

"I guess I would challenge the idea that there are markets in the world that are Australia's markets virtually exclusively, or even ... I would say that there are not markets that are United States' markets," he said.

"To think that because you had a market for a long time that you will always have that market in the face of changing world dynamics I think is pushing it too hard." But the U.S. if pressured by the actions of other countries would use export subsidies, Kleckner said.
"The U.S. does not use export subsidies unless we are forced into it by what other nations are doing. And I would point my finger at the European Union," he said.
Although the European Union used export subsidies on wheat several months ago the U.S had not been pressured into retaliating, Kleckner said.
When the U.S. has wielded export subsidies, they have been at a very low level compared to the Europeans, he said.
